question: A shopkeeper allows a discount of 15% on the marked price of goods and still gains 70% on the whole. Find at what percentage above the cost price does he mark his goods.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

CP over MP = 100-D over 100+P

Where, D = discount%, P = profit%

According to the question,

CP over MP = 100-15 over 100+70

CP over MP = 85 over 170

CP over MP = 1 over 2

Thus, CP:MP = 1:2

The required ratio = (2-1)/1 × 100 = 100%

**Hence, the marked price should be marked at 100% above the cost price.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A shopkeeper allows a discount of 15% on the marked price of goods and still gains 70% on the whole. 

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the goods be 100x

So, selling price = 100x + 100x × 70%

⇒ 170x

According to the question,

Marked price - marked price × 15% = 170x

⇒ 0.85Marked price = 170x

⇒ Marked price = 170x/0.85

⇒ Marked price = 200x

So, extra = 200x - 100x

⇒ 100x

Required % = (100x/100x) × 100

⇒ 100

**∴ He marks his goods at 100% above the cost price.**
